en.name: Halva
en.summary: Sealed and kept cool and dark, a block of sesame halva is usually good for about 1 year, and roughly 1–2 months once you have cut into it. There is no published shelf life for halva, so those figures are read across from tahini, the sesame paste it is made from. Refrigerated, a block will hold about 6 months.
en.pantry: A cool, dark cupboard, sealed, is the right home for halva — about 1 year unopened. Halva is mostly sugar and sesame with almost no free water, which is why it sits unrefrigerated on a shop counter. What ends it is the sesame oil turning rancid — sharp and bitter — not bacteria. Once cut, wrap the face tightly against air and reckon on 1–2 months; keep it away from the stove and out of sunlight, because heat is what drives the rancidity.
en.fridge: About 6 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. That figure is our own reading rather than a published one, and it is worth using for a large slab or a warm kitchen. The cost is real: cold makes halva hard and mutes the flavour, so let it come back to room temperature before eating. Halva studded with fresh pistachio or run through with chocolate keeps less well than the plain kind.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for halva, and it is not a food that needs one. The sugar and the low water content already make it shelf-stable for the better part of a year, and the fridge covers a slab you cannot finish. Freezing does not ruin it, but it buys nothing you cannot get from a cool cupboard and a tight wrapper.
en.thawing: Not normally needed. Bring a refrigerated piece back to room temperature before serving — cold halva is hard and tastes of much less than it should.
spoilage: A sharp, bitter or paint-like taste, which is the sesame oil gone rancid.
A strong oily smell rather than a nutty, toasted one.
Mould at the cut face, which means moisture got in from a wet knife or a damp room.
Any sour or fermented note, unusual in halva and a clear reason to stop.
tips: Cut with a dry knife and press film or foil directly onto the cut face.
Buy by the piece rather than the kilo unless you eat it often.
Oil beading on the surface and a drier, crumblier texture with age are normal.
Keep it away from the hob and out of the sun; heat is what shortens it.

faq.a: About 1 year sealed in a cool, dark cupboard, roughly 1–2 months once cut, or about 6 months refrigerated. No agency publishes a halva figure, so these are read across from tahini and from practice.

faq.q: Does halva need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. It is a dry sugar and sesame confection and keeps at room temperature. The fridge is for a big slab or a hot kitchen, and it makes the halva hard.

faq.q: How can you tell if halva has gone bad?
faq.a: Taste a crumb. Rancid sesame oil is sharply bitter and does not go away. Mould at the cut face or a sour smell are the other reasons to stop.

zh.name: 哈爾瓦芝麻酥糖
zh.summary: 密封、放在陰涼避光處，一塊芝麻哈爾瓦大約可以放 1 年，切開之後大約 1～2 個月。哈爾瓦沒有官方公布的保存期限，上面這些數字是比照它的原料「中東芝麻醬（tahini）」來看的。冷藏的話大約可以放 6 個月。
zh.pantry: 密封、陰涼、避光的櫥櫃就是哈爾瓦該待的地方，未開封大約 1 年。哈爾瓦幾乎全是糖和芝麻，自由水極少，所以它能就這樣擺在店家的櫃檯上不冷藏。終結它的是芝麻油走味那股尖銳的苦，不是細菌。切開之後，把切面緊緊包住隔絕空氣，大約抓 1～2 個月；請遠離爐台、避免日曬，因為熱正是油耗的推手。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下冷藏大約 6 個月。這個數字是我們自己的判斷，不是公開的數據；如果是一大塊，或廚房本來就熱，那就值得這麼做。代價也很實在：低溫會讓哈爾瓦變硬、風味變鈍，所以吃之前要先回到室溫。包了新鮮開心果或夾巧克力的版本，會比原味的更不耐放。
zh.freezer: 哈爾瓦沒有冷凍的期限數據，而它也不是需要冷凍的食物。糖與極低的含水量已經讓它在常溫下撐得住大半年，吃不完的大塊交給冷藏就好。冷凍不會毀了它，但它給不了「陰涼櫥櫃加確實密封」給不了的東西。
zh.thawing: 通常不需要。冷藏過的請先回到室溫再吃——冰冷的哈爾瓦又硬，味道也只剩一半。
spoilage: 嚐起來尖銳發苦或有油漆味，那是芝麻油已經油耗。
聞起來是濃重的油味，而不是烘香的芝麻味。
切面長霉，代表濕氣從沒擦乾的刀子或潮濕的房間跑進去了。
任何酸味或發酵味——哈爾瓦不該有，出現就別吃了。
tips: 用乾燥的刀切，切完把保鮮膜或鋁箔直接壓在切面上。
除非常吃，否則買一塊就好，不要整公斤買。
表面滲油、放久了變得比較乾而鬆碎，都是正常現象。
遠離爐火與陽光，熱是縮短它壽命的主因。

faq.a: 密封放陰涼避光的櫥櫃大約 1 年，切開後約 1～2 個月，冷藏大約 6 個月。沒有機關公布哈爾瓦的數字，這些是比照中東芝麻醬與實務經驗而來。
不需要。它是乾的糖與芝麻製品，常溫就能放。冷藏是為了一大塊吃不完、或廚房太熱的情況，代價是會變硬。
剝一小塊嚐嚐。芝麻油油耗的苦味很尖銳，而且不會消失。切面長霉或有酸味，也是該停手的理由。
